answer_1.quote: In this work, we study a new generation paradigm for LLMs, in which we require LLMs to provide citations to one or a few text passages for any statement they generate.

answer_2.quote: We design automatic evaluation methods in three dimensions: fluency, correctness, and citation quality. Specifically, we use MAUVE to measure fluency, propose tailored correctness metrics for each dataset, and adopt a natural language inference (NLI) model to measure citation quality.

answer_4.quote: To verify that our automatic evaluation correlates with human judgement, we conduct human evaluation on selected models and request workers to judge model generations on three dimensions...
answer_4.guideline: Workers rate utility (1-5 score), judge citation recall (whether cited passages fully support statements), and citation precision (whether citations fully/partially support statements).
